confirmed.statement: (a) The abstract states random assignment of both factors: 'professionals were randomly assigned to work either with or without AI, and either individually or with another professional in new product development teams.' The introduction repeats it: 'randomly assigned to one of four conditions, in a 2x2 experimental design'.

(a) Section 3.2 says: 'Our analyses focus on 776 of these participants who were randomly assigned across four conditions.' It names the four conditions (Control, T1, T2, T3). The form's assignment quote is verbatim from the same paragraph (33 words), and its locator is right.

(a) The next page says 'Randomization was stratified by business unit and geography' and describes Figure 1 'with participants randomly assigned to work either individually or in teams, and with or without AI assistance'. Teams were 'formed by randomly pairing a Commercial and an R&D professional', and one member was randomly designated to submit. Footnote 7 says the geographic part of the clusters served time zones. unit = individual and the eight strata in what_was_assigned are supported.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Section 3.2; pp. 9-10, footnote 7; p. 29, Figure 1

confirmed.statement: preregistered = yes is supported. The title page links AEA RCT Registry trial 13603. Footnote 3 says the study was pre-registered as AEARCTR-0013603 and that the plan becomes public on acceptance or after the registry embargo.

(b) The AI factor gives participants a tool for their own work: 'In the AI-enabled conditions (T2 and T3), participants received a one-hour training session on how to prompt and interact with the GenAI tool for CPG-related tasks.' Each individual or team then submitted its own solution. All prompts and responses were recorded, and Section 6.4 measures how many AI sentences stayed in the submitted solutions. The arms differ in how participants produced their own solutions, not only in whose output is rated, and evaluators were blind to condition.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Section 3.2; p. 4, Section 1; p. 11, Section 3.3; p. 18, Section 6.4; p. 13, Section 4.2; p. 49, Appendix B.4

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is a large language model: 'The GenAI tool used in the experiment was built on GPT-4 and accessed through Microsoft Azure.' Footnote 10 says participants at the July workshop had GPT-4o. ai_tool.name_model matches.

ai_tool.role = open_chat and how_used match the text. One of the authors led the training and gave a PDF of recommended prompts. Appendix C says the prompts help participants work 'using the AI as they saw fit', and its prompts are instructions to the model, not ready-made ideas. Footnote 13 reports 18.7 prompts on average among participants who kept some AI text.
confirmed.locator: p. 10, Section 3.2; p. 50, Appendix C; pp. 51-53, Appendix C.6-C.7; p. 19, footnote 13

confirmed.statement: (d) The comparison arms match the form. Control is 'Individual without AI' (ai = none). T1 is a team without AI with a randomly paired human partner, which the form spec codes as other_aid. Both no-AI arms got the GenAI training only after the scored task. So T2 versus Control and T3 versus T1 differ in AI access bundled with the training and prompt PDF, as what_was_assigned says. T2 versus T1 is AI versus a human partner (ai_vs_active).
confirmed.locator: p. 9, Section 3.2; p. 10, Section 3.2; p. 11, Section 3.3; form-spec.md, field note on arms[].ai; creativity-codebook.md, section 5

confirmed.statement: The arm counts match Table 1: 154 (Individual No AI), 155 (Individual + AI), 230 in 115 teams (Team No AI), and 252 in 126 teams (Team + AI). Their units sum to the 550 solutions in Table 2. The paper prints no count at assignment, so arms[].n_randomized = null is right.

(e) No coded estimate is within-person. The paper says 'all the primary results presented in this study are based on the between subject comparisons, focusing on the initial performance across all conditions before any crossover occurred.' The control groups' repeat with AI had a fixed order (no AI first), and no crossover result appears anywhere in pp. 1-54. structure = between is right for the coded estimates.

The task is an ideation task, as criterion 1 requires: participants developed 'viable ideas for new products, packaging, communication approaches, or retail execution' for real business-unit problems.
The 'AI Only' curve in Figure 13 is GPT-4o output from the problem instructions, not an assigned arm. The form keeps it out of arms and marks its row as not a randomized contrast.
confirmed.locator: p. 19, Section 6.4 and footnote 14; p. 40, Figure 13

confirmed.statement: Caveat, not recorded in the form, no code change for criterion 1. Table 1 shows the AI split is balanced on function within each format (R&D share 0.604 vs 0.594 for individuals, 0.500 vs 0.500 for teams). The individual arms hold more R&D staff than the team arms (about 0.60 vs exactly 0.500) and have longer tenure (12.351 and 11.816 vs 10.091 and 10.476 years). So the final split into individual and team arms is not independent of function, and the document does not say how the split handled it. Table 1 tests balance only within each format. This bears on the ai_vs_active rows (Individual + AI vs Team No AI), not on the AI contrasts.

Caveat, recorded in the form. When one member of a team did not take part, the team was nullified and the other member was moved to an individual assignment. The paper does not say how many people moved, or whether they kept their AI condition.

Caveat, recorded in the form. 811 people attended and 35 were not randomized. All 35 worked alone: late entrants without AI, staff above band 3 with AI. That leaves 776, but the Table 1 arms sum to 791 people. The document does not reconcile the counts, so up to 15 non-randomized people could be in the individual arms. Footnote 6 says results are consistent when the non-randomized participants are included. Criterion 1 stands under either count.
confirmed.locator: p. 9, Section 3.2 and footnote 6; p. 41, Table 1

confirmed.statement: Caveat, not recorded in the form, no code change. The paper describes no check that the no-AI arms did not use AI on their own during the virtual workshop. Table 1 shows that 71 to 81 percent of each arm had ChatGPT access at work. The arms are labeled 'without AI' throughout, and the form follows the labels.
The file is NBER Working Paper 33641 (April 2025). The 2026 Organization Science version is not on file, so its assignment text could not be checked.
confirmed.locator: pp. 1-2; retrieval.json entry c052 (no version_saved field)

summary: The PDF supports every part of the assignment, arms, and ai_tool coding: P&G professionals were randomly assigned, within business-unit by geography strata, to work alone or in a randomly paired team, with or without a GPT-4-based tool plus prompt training, on a product-ideation task (pp. 2, 4, 9-10, 29), and every coded estimate is between-subject (p. 11). Four caveats leave criterion 1 intact because the AI split itself is balanced (Table 1, p. 41): the individual and team arms differ in R&D share and tenure, an unstated number of team members moved to individual arms (p. 10, fn. 8), the 776 randomized do not reconcile with the 791 people in the analyzed arms (p. 9; p. 41), and no check on AI use in the no-AI arms is described.
